title: Forms and Validation Styles
summary: Bootstrap can style text fields, choices and labels. Clear HTML labels still give each field its meaning.
introduction: Bootstrap can style text fields, choices and labels. Clear HTML labels still give each field its meaning. Build one labelled field first. Then add a select box and a check box, making sure each has words that explain its job.
learningObjectives: Style text inputs, selects, textareas, checks and switches with the form classes
Lay out forms with the grid, floating labels and input groups
Show valid and invalid states with was-validated, is-invalid and feedback elements
Keep every label connected to its field so the form stays accessible

blocks.text: Text-like inputs and `<textarea>` take `.form-control`, which makes them block-level, full width, with a light grey border, rounded corners and a blue focus ring. Labels take `.form-label` for a small bottom margin, help text takes `.form-text`, and each label-plus-field pair usually sits in a `div.mb-3` to space the rows. The `for` and `id` pair is not a Bootstrap requirement but an HTML one: it is what connects the label to the field for screen readers and makes the label clickable.

blocks.title: A basic form
blocks.code: We never share your email with anyone else.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Each label sits above a full-width field with a 1px light grey (#dee2e6) border and 6px rounded corners
Small grey help text under the email field; the three rows are 16px apart
Clicking into a field turns its border light blue and adds a soft blue glow (a 4px box shadow)
A blue Send button below the textarea

blocks.text: A `<select>` takes `.form-select`, not `.form-control`, because it needs its own arrow icon. Checkboxes and radios are wrapped in `.form-check` with `.form-check-input` on the input and `.form-check-label` on the label; add `.form-switch` to the wrapper to turn a checkbox into a toggle switch, and `.form-check-inline` to put several side by side. Sliders use `.form-range`.

blocks.title: Select, checkbox, radios and a switch
Rendered result
blocks.content:
A full-width drop-down showing "Choose…" with a grey chevron on the right
A square checkbox with its label to the right; ticking it fills the box blue with a white tick
"Post" (selected, blue circle with a white dot) and "Pick up" on one line
A pill-shaped switch with a grey knob on the left; clicking slides the knob right and turns the pill blue

blocks.text: `.form-floating` places the label *inside* the field and floats it to the top when the field has focus or a value. The markup order is strict: the input comes first, the label second, and the input must carry a `placeholder` (any text; it is hidden) because the effect relies on the `:placeholder-shown` selector. `.input-group` glues a text addon or a button to a field, for example a currency symbol or a search button.

blocks.title: Floating label and input groups
blocks.code: £ .00

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
A tall (58px) field showing "Email address" in grey inside it; on focus or when text is typed, the label shrinks and moves to the top edge while the text sits below it
A number field with a grey "£" box joined to its left and a grey ".00" box joined to its right, sharing borders
A search field with an outlined Search button attached to its right edge

blocks.text: Laying out forms with the grid

Forms use the same rows and columns as everything else. `row g-3` spaces fields both horizontally and vertically, and `col-md-6` puts two fields on one line from tablets upward while keeping them stacked on phones. For a horizontal form, where the label sits to the left of the field, use `.col-form-label` on the label so its padding lines up with the input.

blocks.title: Two fields per row on medium screens
Rendered result
blocks.content:
Below 768px: four rows stacked, 16px apart: First name, Last name, Address, Save
768px and wider: First name and Last name side by side at half width each, then Address full width, then the Save button

blocks.text: Bootstrap can colour a field green or red and show a message under it, but it never decides *when*. Its styles are triggered in one of two ways. **Client side**, the styles key off the browser's own `:valid` and `:invalid` state, but only once the form has the class `was-validated`; you add that class in a submit handler after calling `checkValidity()`. **Server side**, you render the field with `.is-valid` or `.is-invalid` directly. In both cases the message lives in a `.valid-feedback` or `.invalid-feedback` element placed right after the field; it is hidden until the matching state applies.

blocks.title: Client-side validation with feedback messages
blocks.code:
Please enter your name.
You must be 18 or older.
Looks good!

blocks.title: Behaviour in the browser
blocks.content:
Before the first submit: plain grey-bordered fields, no messages
Submit with both fields empty: both fields get a red border and a red icon; "Please enter your name." and "You must be 18 or older." appear in red; the form is not sent
Type a name and 25, submit again: both fields get a green border and a tick icon, "Looks good!" appears in green under Age, and the form is sent

blocks.text: The `novalidate` attribute matters: it stops the browser from showing its own validation bubbles and blocking the submit event, which would mean your handler never runs and `was-validated` is never added. The server-side variant needs no script at all:

blocks.title: Server-rendered invalid state
blocks.code: That username is already taken.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content: The field has a red border and a red icon on the right, and the red message is visible immediately, with no JavaScript involved

blocks.title: Common mistake: feedback that never appears
blocks.text: Two things silently break validation messages. First, a `.invalid-feedback` element is only displayed when it is a **sibling placed immediately after** a field that is invalid, so wrapping the field in an extra `<div>` or putting the message before the input hides it for ever. Second, forgetting `novalidate` means the browser blocks invalid submissions itself, your submit handler does not run, and the `was-validated` class is never added, so Bootstrap's styles never switch on.

blocks.title: Validation is not security
blocks.text: Everything in this lesson is presentation. The `required` and `min` attributes and the green and red borders help honest users; anyone can bypass them with the developer tools. The server must validate again before it trusts a single value.

questions.question: Client-side validation styles only appear after the class `___` has been added to the form element.
questions.explanation: was-validated switches on the :valid and :invalid based styles. Your submit handler adds it after calling checkValidity().

questions.question: Inside `.form-floating`, the `<label>` must come after the `<input>`.
questions.explanation: The floating effect uses a sibling selector from the input to the label, so the input must come first and must have a placeholder attribute.
